sources.title: Associates Program Operating Agreement
sources.page_says: Page header: 'Updated: October 15, 2025'. Section 1 defines 'Special Links' as the tagged link formats Amazon provides. Section 5 requires the statement 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.' on the Site, and bars expressing or implying that Amazon supports, sponsors or endorses the Associate.
sources.supports: Disclosure wording (C-01), Special Links definition (C-06), no endorsement implication (C-09)
sources.reverified_result: Re-fetched 2026-11-20. Confirmed: "Updated: October 15, 2025"; §5 wording "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases."; no tag= parameter in final URL.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies (Commission Income Statement, Section 2 disqualifications)
sources.page_says: Page header: 'Updated: April 14, 2026'. Section 2 lists disqualified purchases, including (e) referrals through a 'Redirecting Link' that sends users indirectly via an intermediate site without an affirmative action, and (g) purchases 'not correctly tracked or reported because the links from your site to the relevant Amazon Site are not properly formatted'. The commission rate table is in an Appendix that links to SRC-04.
sources.supports: Link-format review (FLG-R01, FLG-R03, Q-02), commission appendix pointer (FLG-R05)

sources.title: Why do I have to identify myself as an Associate? How should I do this on social media?
sources.page_says: Requires (1) a link-level disclosure that is clear, e.g. '(paid link)' or '#ad', and placed near any affiliate link or product review; and (2) the Section 5 statement on the Site. Points to the FTC Disclosures 101 guide.

sources.title: Associates Program Commission Income Statement Appendix (Standard Commission Income)
sources.page_says: Fetch returned Amazon's sign-in page instead of the rate table. The rate table could not be read.
sources.supports: Commission potential (FLG-R05, Q-06). No rates are shown on this site.

sources.title: Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers
sources.page_says: Disclose a material connection; place the disclosure where it is 'hard to miss' and with the endorsement itself; do not rely on About or profile pages, or on text hidden behind 'more'; use clear terms such as 'ad', 'sponsored'; do not make claims that would need proof you do not have. Page is dated November 2019.

sources.title: GitHub Pages limits
sources.page_says: 'GitHub Pages is not intended for or allowed to be used as a free web-hosting service to run your online business, e-commerce site, or any other website that is primarily directed at either facilitating commercial transactions or providing commercial software as a service.' Soft limits: 100 GB bandwidth per month; 1 GB maximum site size. Static hosting only.
sources.supports: Hosting acceptable-use review (FLG-R09), size and bandwidth (repo review)

sources.title: Configuring a publishing source for your GitHub Pages site
sources.page_says: A publishing source can be a branch with either the root (/) or a /docs folder. Built-in Jekyll is the default when publishing from a branch; a .nojekyll file is commonly used with other build output. Pages sites are public even if the repository is private.

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google (rel="sponsored")
sources.page_says: Use rel="sponsored" for links that are advertisements or paid placements (paid links). Multiple values may be space-separated. Last updated 2025-12-10 UTC.

sources.title: Sitemaps XML format (sitemaps.org protocol)
sources.page_says: Each <url> needs a <loc>; lastmod should be the date the page was last modified; all URLs must be from a single host; entity-escape &, <, > and quotes.

sources.title: RSS 2.0 Specification
sources.page_says: Required channel elements: title, link, description. Item pubDate uses RFC 822 date-time format. The rss element must carry version="2.0".
